advice.claim: Business owners must use facts and data to guide their decisions and understand their business performance.
advice.quote: You cannot move forward. You're like a ship. We are like a ship without a compass. How do we go in that direction if we don't know where we've been?

advice.claim: Do not base your business model on the behavior of a small minority of customers who abuse your policies.
advice.quote: Never build a platform of business around what 3% do.

advice.claim: Focus on whether a customer will pay to use a service again as the primary metric for success.
advice.quote: Will you pay me to use it again?

advice.claim: Do not punish the majority of your customers because of the actions of a small percentage who abuse your policies.
advice.quote: Why would we punish 97% of our customers for what 3% do?

advice.claim: Do not create overly complex membership structures or rules based on the fear of a small percentage of customers abusing the system.
advice.quote: Sometimes we build memberships and packages around 3%. We're so afraid that they're going to abuse the process that we start saying unlimited tanning. you can tan up to eight sessions a month. Unlimited sunless, up to four times a month. We start attaching all of these streams.

advice.claim: Build business processes based on the behavior of the majority of your customers rather than the minority.
advice.quote: So when we're building processes, build them around what the amount of people, the larger amount of people will use, without accurate knowledge about our brand's performance, and we're really, really gonna, we're just gonna beat this thing to death this afternoon.

advice.claim: Adding a single month to a customer's contract length can significantly increase revenue without increasing overhead costs.
advice.quote: You made $100,000 for free by adding one extra month to the length of how long they stayed with you.

advice.claim: Offering alternative services like wellness can help retain customers who might otherwise leave the business.
advice.quote: And then eventually what did they buy? They bought a mystic pen, right? Because it was an alternative that represented a new modality that kept your customer.

advice.claim: Proactive planning and investment during stable times are necessary to survive economic downturns.
advice.quote: If we're not investing in new equipment, if we're not thinking about new strategies, if we're not looking at our numbers when it's calm, we're gonna get destroyed when there's a storm.

advice.claim: Analyze your business data and metrics during slow periods to prepare for and survive difficult economic times.
advice.quote: if we're not looking at our numbers when it's calm, we're gonna get destroyed when there's a storm.

advice.claim: Ensure your team identifies specific, actionable takeaways from industry events to improve the brand.
advice.quote: they will have to come away with five takeaways that we can improve on or better ourselves

advice.claim: Use trade shows as an opportunity to have honest conversations with vendors about equipment needs and business goals.
advice.quote: This is an opportunity to start conversations with people about how we can improve our brand. I want new equipment. I'm not sure I can afford new equipment. Have that conversation. I want new equipment. I'm not sure what equipment. Have the conversation.

advice.claim: It is easier to win market share by taking customers from competitors than by trying to acquire new ones.
advice.quote: It is far easier to steal a customer than earn one.

advice.claim: Charge a facility fee for memberships to cover costs and generate significant revenue from recurring fees.
advice.quote: every membership is charged an annual 30 facility fee and it's on their first draft following their first month

advice.claim: Implementing a facility fee is an effective way to generate revenue and cover costs without significant customer pushback.
advice.quote: The easiest thing you can do is add a facility fee.

advice.claim: Explain the value of the facility fee by linking it to specific equipment or services provided.
advice.quote: When they see it at work, they're glad to do it.

advice.claim: Increase revenue by encouraging existing customers to purchase additional months of service.
advice.quote: If we can get those customers that we already have to buy an extra month or an extra two months, think about what that means.

advice.claim: Keep the sales process simple to ensure staff can close sales effectively.
advice.quote: Did we make packages? Did we make the presentations too difficult? And then we go back and we adjust to make it simpler.

advice.claim: Position your business as a wellness spa rather than just a tanning salon to improve employee morale and perception.
advice.quote: She goes home. How job search go today? I got a job at the wellness spa.

advice.claim: Ensure your physical location and branding immediately communicate your value to customers because they make decisions based on visual cues within seconds.
advice.quote: When you walk into your store, is what you see what you get?

advice.claim: Avoid making excuses for customers who leave without buying; if they walk out, it is because the visual environment or initial presentation failed to engage them.
advice.quote: If they walk out of your store, they did it because we did something wrong.

advice.claim: Incorporate service modalities that do not require staff labor to manage high labor costs.
advice.quote: The smallest modalities should include services exempt from labor.

advice.claim: Use wellness services to complement tanning services and attract a broader customer base.
advice.quote: We're trying to get them into different modalities to complement what they do. We've had so many people that have come in for other services that became light light therapy customers just because of the wellness services they make.

advice.claim: Train staff to present a professional, high-end image because customers judge the business based on the appearance of the staff.
advice.quote: If that's the case, why don't we take that philosophy and apply it to our stores if we know that the person behind the counter sells the person in front of the counter why don't we capitalize on that you see the value of having the sales staff trained to look and feel the party that becomes critical
